label: Voice interaction
tagline: Makes the prototype speak text computed at run time, and listen back
description: The RUNTIME sibling of sound-orchestrator. Where sound-orchestrator bakes .mp3 assets ahead of time, this orchestrator builds the voice UX layer of a running prototype: speaking text nobody knew at build time (what the user typed, what just changed, what the app computed) and listening to the user. Surveys the built prototype for voice-worthy surfaces and classifies each as speak-on-demand, speak-on-event or a conversational loop, commits a voice UX design (persona cast from the shared sound-library voice map, speak-trigger map with queue / interrupt / coalesce policy, mic flow with denial fallback, fallback copy), gates the design and its per-utterance cost with the user, then dispatches one voice-ux-author drawer that bakes woven-voice.js plus a project-specific voice-layer.js into the prototype and wires the affordances. Speech runs through the daemon's /__voice/tts and /__voice/stt (share-scoped twins at /s/<token>/api/voice/*), so keys never reach the browser. Degrades by design rather than aborting: no ElevenLabs key ships the same layer on the browser's speechSynthesis, no transcription engine hides the mic affordance. Runs LATE, after the core build and visual passes. Cold-isolated per prototype.

hardRule.header: Runtime voice: dispatch voice-interaction-orchestrator when the prototype itself should speak or listen
hardRule.body:
Voice as STRUCTURE, not as an asset. The dividing line against sound-orchestrator is what the words are: a narrated intro that is identical every visit is a baked .mp3 and belongs to sound-orchestrator; anything the prototype has to say about what just happened belongs here. A brief can want both.

- **Trigger A - explicit request.** "make it talk", "read the results aloud", "add a voice assistant", "let me dictate", "voice control", "narrate what changes".
- **Trigger B - the brief commits to spoken interaction.** An assistant, a hands-free / eyes-busy context (driving, kitchen, workshop), a language tool, an accessibility-first surface. Dispatch even when the user did not use the word voice.
- **Trigger C - the interesting output is dynamic text** where hearing it lands differently from reading it.

The key is a SOFT gate, not a hard one. `GET /__voice/status` reports tts and stt availability; with no ElevenLabs key the orchestrator builds the same layer on the browser's own speech synthesis and says so at its design gate. Never silently skip voice because a key is missing - tell the user what they would gain by wiring one.

```
Task(subagent_type: "voice-interaction-orchestrator",
     description: "Design and build the prototype's voice layer",
     prompt: "<envelope per voice-interaction-orchestrator.md §1 - projectId, branch, prototypeSlug, committedAesthetic, explicitDirection, sensoryTargets, voiceStatus, soundRegister>")
```

It runs LATE (after the core build and the visual passes, alongside or after polish, before final QA), surveys the voice-worthy surfaces, stops at a `cp_vx_gate_<projectId>` decision-request covering the design AND the per-utterance cost (relay it verbatim), then hands back a `vx_voice_<slug>` builder plus a `qa_gate_vx_<projectId>` gate for you to chain-run.

When it lands, tell the user both surprising truths: the first spoken line needs a click or keypress first (browsers block audio before a gesture), and a SHARED prototype speaks with real voices only after they switch Voice on for that share (it spends their ElevenLabs credits, so it is off by default and rate-capped when on).

- ❌ Hand-wire `fetch('/__voice/tts')` in chat - the baked woven-voice.js already solves endpoint resolution, share paths, queueing, the gesture unlock and fallback tiering.
- ❌ Bake .mp3 files for text that changes at run time - that is what this orchestrator exists to avoid.
- ❌ Request the microphone at page load. The permission prompt belongs to a button the user pressed.

triggers.title: Runtime voice layer (LATE - after the core build and visual passes)
triggers.rule: After the prototype is built and the visual passes are done, dispatch voice-interaction-orchestrator when the user asked for speech or voice control, when the brief commits to spoken interaction (assistant, hands-free context, language tool, accessibility-first surface), or when the prototype's interesting output is dynamic text worth hearing. The ElevenLabs key is a SOFT gate: without one it ships the same layer on the browser's speechSynthesis and says so at its design gate, so never skip it silently for a missing key. It stops at a design + cost decision card; relay that verbatim. Fixed narration / sound effects / music beds are sound-orchestrator's job, not this one's.
